message: No detected input validation: No schema checks, dtype assertions, or value-range guards are applied to incoming data or command-line arguments before use.
No detected untrusted source handling: Data is loaded from local CSV/NPZ files with no checksum verification, authentication, or integrity checks; no remote sources are fetched in this code.
No detected label flipping detection: No code checks label distributions, validates label values against an expected set, or uses any label-noise detection tool before training.
No detected data poisoning defenses: No outlier detection, statistical anomaly checks, or filtering of suspicious inputs is performed on the training data anywhere in the shown code.

No detected model integrity verification: The code loads data and runs model training/inference (e.g., np.loadtxt, pickle.load, np.load) without any hash checks, signature verification, or pinned revision controls on pretrained weights or serialized models.
No detected label distribution validation: No code checks class balance, expected label sets, or anomalous sample detection before or during training in any of the files.
No detected backdoor or trigger detection: There is no neural-cleanse, activation-pattern analysis, gradient anomaly detection, or any other backdoor/trigger defense in the training loops.
No detected differential privacy: No differential privacy libraries (Opacus, TensorFlow Privacy, DP-SGD) or DP mechanisms are used anywhere in the training code.
No detected adversarial robustness testing: No adversarial robustness testing libraries (Foolbox, ART, FGSM, PGD) or any adversarial stress tests are used anywhere in the evaluation code.

No detected metric tampering protection: While separate train/test data paths are used, there is no signing, hashing, or cryptographic verification of evaluation data, and no mechanism to prevent metric manipulation or ensure test set isolation from training influence.

No detected input sanitization: Command-line arguments are used directly (e.g., sys.argv indices passed straight to subprocess.call and os.path joins) with no shape, range, type, or schema validation applied to inputs before model execution.

No detected output bounds checks: Model outputs (ITE, ATE, PEHE, RMSE, etc.) are printed and aggregated with np.mean/np.abs but there are no NaN guards, range checks, or sanity bounds applied before returning or saving results.

No detected prompt injection defenses: The models used (CFRNet, CEVAE, SITE, DRN, BART, CForest) are causal inference/tabular ML models, not LLMs, so prompt-injection defenses are not applicable and none are present.
